mod-description: Gear-driven workshop machines and limited automation.
handbook-text-fluid-pipe-copper:
Carries liquid or steam through connected ports. Full pipes can carry flow through a connected outlet. Longer runs and uphill routes reduce delivery; use a shorter supply line or more pump pressure for faster flow. Gravity moves liquid downhill; a pump can lift it against gravity. Blocked lines retain liquid and build pressure. Steam compresses much more easily and flows by pressure without water-column weight. Place it against the face it should connect to; sneak while placing to open the opposite face instead. Use a wrench on a face to open or close that port.

rightmouse a free face with plain glass, a Steel Sprinkler (bottom face only), a Copper Pipe Nozzle (any face), or a copper plate (an open port facing air). Sneak and rightmouse with an empty hand to remove a fitting.

rightmouse with one plank to fit a wooden frame. Frames join neighboring frames without gaps, with collars around pipe ends and one diagonal brace on each empty side and bottom. The sparse top supports a barrel whenever there is no pipe above. An upward connection leaves a gap for the barrel nozzle.

Add one more plank to insulate the frame with crate panels. The insulated pipe counts as a full block for rooms and attachments and blocks daylight. Pipe connections and fittings still work; the panels cover inspection windows. An open frame alone does not seal a room. Sneak and rightmouse with an empty hand to recover the lining plank first, then click the wood to recover the frame plank. Breaking the pipe returns both installed planks and its fittings in survival.

Creative mode: find it in the Gearwright tab.
handbook-text-creative-fluid-pump:
Creative-only source for a connected Copper Pipe. rightmouse to choose liquid or steam and set 0-1000 kPa; 0 stops the source.

Find it in the Gearwright creative tab.
handbook-text-passive-fluid-pump: Legacy block with no current function. Use a Copper Pipe Nozzle to connect a pipe to an unsealed liquid container.
handbook-text-sprinkler-brass:
rightmouse the bottom face of a Copper Pipe to attach it. Water reaches farmland one to four blocks below; higher pressure increases its circular reach from one to four blocks. Steam will not pass through it, and other liquids kill affected crops.

Creative mode: find it in the Gearwright tab.
handbook-text-irrigator-pipe-bronze:
Place in a straight horizontal run below solid ceiling blocks; it follows the direction you face and connects at its ends. It waters the first farmland one to four blocks below its three outlets, up to 80% moisture. Steam will not irrigate, and other liquids kill affected crops. See the Copper Pipe for a configurable supply line.

Creative mode: find it in the Gearwright tab.
handbook-text-fluid-pipe-intake-copper:
rightmouse any free face of a Copper Pipe to attach it. It transfers liquid to or from an adjacent unsealed container. Point it into a natural level-7 liquid source and apply at least -70 kPa to draw liquid without removing the source block. This requires pump-driven suction: a passive water column or tall empty pipe run cannot generate extraction vacuum. Lifting from below still costs pressure, and suction rebuilds after loading. Pointing it sideways or down into open air deletes liquid; pointing it up releases overflow only. Sneak and rightmouse with an empty hand to remove it.

Creative mode: find it in the Gearwright tab.
handbook-text-pottery-profile-tool: Creative-only item with no gameplay action. Find it in the Gearwright creative tab.
handbook-text-small-flywheel:
Place inline with a horizontal Wooden Axle; the 3 by 3 by 1 space around its shaft must be clear. It stores momentum while the network speeds up and returns it when the network slows. When isolated it keeps a one-block mechanical network, then automatically joins a compatible drivetrain that reconnects. It does not create power, and each flywheel adds resistance.

Creative mode: find it in the Gearwright tab.
handbook-text-overrunning-transmission:
Place it inline by clicking the source-side axle; that side becomes the input. Its two ends remain separate mechanical networks. The ratchet transfers rotation while the input is faster. Once locked, it tolerates a small output-side speed lead and releases only when the output becomes measurably faster. Under load, tooth-phase correction grows as a pawl approaches its locking face so the live parts do not pass through each other. Reverse rotation works automatically: the brass tooth ramps and all three pawls mirror together. The open frame shows the live mechanism without a hidden transmission inside. Break and replace the block from the other end to change which axle is the input.

Creative mode: find it in the Gearwright tab.
handbook-text-lateral-crank:
Place it on its own or inline with a horizontal Wooden Axle; it aligns to a neighboring axle when one is present. The wooden shaft, iron crank web, and bronze journal rotate together in the same direction as the connected Wooden Axle and stop with that network. The pump's connecting rod rocks between the orbiting journal and sliding piston. With no pump attached, rightmouse it with an empty hand to advance its drive phase by 45 degrees; each drive shaft keeps its own phase. It renders one cantilevered side when only one axle is connected and adds the second cheek only between two axles. Attach one Reciprocating Pump to any face perpendicular to the shaft.

Creative mode: find it in the Gearwright tab.
handbook-text-reciprocating-pump:
The pump can be placed before its drive. The face used for placement becomes its drive face; place a Reciprocating Drive Shaft against that face later. If placed beside a free compatible drive journal, the pump aligns to it automatically. The copper-rimmed side is the input and the full bronze-rimmed side is the output; sneak while placing to swap them. Both pipe connections are centered on their block faces. Shaft motion, piston position, wet checks, and chamber fill share the same server timing, including when the drive stops. Wet checks open with actual flow. The rod stays pinned to the drive journal and sliding piston in every mounting direction. The piston travels six model units; chamber volume follows its height. The upstroke draws available contents from the input pipe into the 4 L glass chamber; the pipe does not need to be full. A short, charged intake with positive supply pressure can fill the chamber on each stroke even at higher shaft speeds. More speed needs more supply; use gravity head or active pumping to feed it. The glass, liquid top surface, and chamber-content tooltip show the stored amount. The liquid reaches the basin walls and floor; a filled chamber meets the piston underside. The downstroke closes the inlet and delivers liquid as the piston reduces the chamber volume, stopping at outlet pressure balance. Water does not visually drain ahead of the piston crossing the empty space above it. Delivery pauses during the upstroke; the output check does not draw liquid back. A full pipe can carry delivery onward through connected pipes and an available outlet. A sealed, disconnected, or overpressured line traps liquid and raises back-pressure without deleting it. Above the 1500 kPa service pressure, resistance rises rapidly but stays finite, slowing or stalling the drivetrain according to its power. Resistance is checked throughout the stroke, so a blocked pump can stop during compression on a large or fast geared drivetrain. A nearly empty chamber reaches its liquid later in the downstroke. The shaft and piston hold the stopped position together. Positive pressure resists contraction, not the expanding half after bottom dead centre. There is no forced shaft lock or automatic pressure-relief fluid loss. Unblocking the outlet lets a pressurized chamber drain even while stationary. Steam and all container liquids are supported. A Copper Pipe Nozzle can draw from a natural level-7 liquid source only below -70 kPa, reserving at least 70 J of drive work per litre. Dry intake runs carry suction to the source over successive steps; longer runs and lifting from below can take more strokes to prime and fill less of the chamber each cycle.

The low wooden cradle appears only with the drive shaft above the pump and a solid support below it.
handbook-text-controlled-clutch: Gearwright keeps the shafts on the two ends of this transmission as separate mechanical networks. An adjacent Clutch exchanges rotation between them while engaged without joining or rebuilding either network. Disengaging it stops the exchange but leaves both networks intact.
flywheel-state-read-only: Flywheel inertia is disabled because its saved state uses an unsupported schema.
controlled-clutch-waiting: Waiting for a mechanical network on both shaft ends.
controlled-clutch-bypassed: Both ends are already joined by another mechanical path.
lateral-crank-angle-locked: Remove the attached pump before changing the drive phase.
lateral-crank-state-read-only: Drive phase changes are disabled because its saved state uses an unsupported schema.
reciprocating-pump-status-disconnected: The reciprocating drive shaft is disconnected.
reciprocating-pump-status-dead-center: Piston is at a dead centre.
reciprocating-pump-status-output-blocked: The output pipe is disconnected or blocked.
reciprocating-pump-status-output-overpre: Service pressure exceeded: drive resistance rises rapidly. Contents are retained.
hydraulic-status-state-read-only: Transfers paused: a connected pipe has an unsupported saved state.
reciprocating-pump-state-read-only: Pumping is disabled because its saved state uses an unsupported schema.
block-placefailure-gearwright-reciprocat: Only one pump can use a reciprocating drive journal.
The nearby pump and axle require different drive-shaft directions.
pipe-content-conflict: That change would join pipe networks containing different contents.
block-placefailure-gearwright-irrigator-: The Irrigator Pipe cannot be supported at that location.
hydraulic-status-flow-solving: Flow paused: pressure could not settle within the simulation limit. The network will retry.
hydraulic-status-network-too-large: Flow paused: this connected network exceeds the 4096-cell simulation limit. Split it into smaller runs.
hydraulic-status-running: Pipe network is settling pressure and contents.
hydraulic-status-waiting-for-chunks: Waiting for connected chunks to load.
hydraulic-status-mixed-content: Connected pipes contain different contents; transfer is stopped.
hydraulic-status-mixed-sources: Different sources are trying to fill this empty network.
hydraulic-status-content-mismatch: A connected source or container has the wrong content.
hydraulic-status-gas-container-blocked: Steam cannot enter a Vintage Story liquid container.
hydraulic-status-invalid-content: The selected pipe content is unavailable.
hydraulic-status-no-source: No usable liquid container is connected.
hydraulic-status-reserve-reached: The old horizontal reserve has been reached.
hydraulic-status-deprecated: This Gravity Drain is deprecated; use a Copper Pipe Nozzle.
